title: Minimum Number of Platforms
statement:
A railway station receives `n` trains. Train `i` arrives at time `arr[i]` and departs at time `dep[i]`, where `arr[i] ≤ dep[i]`. Times are plain integers.

Each train occupies one platform for the whole time interval from `arr[i]` to `dep[i]`, **both ends included**. Two trains cannot share a platform at the same moment, so a train that arrives at exactly the time another train departs needs a **different** platform from it.

Find the **minimum number of platforms** the station needs so that no train ever has to wait.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `arr[0] ... arr[n-1]`.
The third line contains `n` integers `dep[0] ... dep[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the minimum number of platforms.

examples.explanation: Train 0 stays from 100 to 200, so trains 1 and 2 each overlap with it, but train 1 leaves at 135 before train 2 arrives at 140. At most two trains are in the station at once.

Train 0 leaves at 20 exactly when train 1 arrives, and the end points count, so they overlap at time 20. Likewise trains 1 and 2 overlap at time 30, but there is never a moment with three trains present.
All five trains are in the station at time 5.

hints: The answer is the largest number of trains present at the same instant. The maximum is always reached at the moment some train arrives.
Sort the arrival times and the departure times separately. You do not need to keep track of which departure belongs to which arrival.

Sweep through arrivals in order with a second pointer over the sorted departures: a departure strictly before the current arrival frees a platform. Track the maximum of (arrivals so far - freed platforms).
